governanceNotes: Authored conservatively at ASSOCIATION_ONLY strength: both quantified prevalence cohorts (68.2% n=157 Polish otosclerosis series; 72.7% n=66 Portuguese series) are otosclerosis populations, so the edge generalizes the conductive-deprivation mechanism to other conductive etiologies without equivalent cohort evidence for them.

Severity-decoupling guard recorded in-file: both cohorts report tinnitus severity NOT correlating with audiometric degree (Lima 2022 explicitly; Skarzynski 2019 p>0.05), and Deggouj records prevalence improvement after corrective surgery, so presence, laterality, and severity must each be individually documented rather than inferred from the hearing-loss rating.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: The validated-questionnaire otosclerosis cohort found preoperative tinnitus in 107 of 157 patients (68.2%), 47.7% unilateral in the surgical ear and 52.3% bilateral, moderately severe on THI/TFI instruments (Skarzynski 2019); the Portuguese acuphenometry cohort found tinnitus in 72.7% of 66 otosclerosis patients, mostly unilateral and low-frequency, with THI median 37 (mild handicap modal, severe 22.9%) (Lima 2022); the literature review identifies middle-ear and secondary inner-ear dysfunction from stapes blockage as the major etiopathogenic factors and documents considerable tinnitus-prevalence improvement after corrective surgery, indicating a substantial reversible conductive component (Deggouj 2009).
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation is established at the mapping level: the cohorts are otosclerosis-specific rather than all-cause conductive-loss populations, tinnitus severity does not correlate with hearing-loss degree in either cohort, cochlear (sensorineural) involvement can coexist and independently generate tinnitus, and surgery-improvement data show reversible contributions - so no directional claim is made here.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: A conductive-deprivation/middle-ear-dysfunction pathway is hypothesized: ossicular fixation or deficit attenuates energy delivery to the cochlea, and the resulting auditory deprivation plus possible secondary inner-ear involvement from stapes blockage produces limited, partly reversible central-auditory-pathway changes experienced as tinnitus; stapes surgery reduces tinnitus prevalence, consistent with a conductive contribution. The cohorts are otosclerosis-specific and severity is decoupled from hearing-loss degree, so no directional claim is made here.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: This relationship is supported as an association only. Tinnitus accompanies conductive hearing loss in roughly two-thirds of otosclerosis cohorts; individual determination requires audiometric documentation of the conductive component, tinnitus characterization with chronology, exclusion of independent tinnitus generators, and review by a qualified medical professional.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: validated audiometric documentation of the conductive loss with air-bone gap and chronology; tinnitus characterization (laterality, pitch, loudness) with onset relative to the hearing loss; exclusion of sensorineural, noise-induced, ototoxic, and presbycusis contributors; otologic examination identifying the conductive mechanism (otosclerosis, chronic otitis media, ossicular chain); a medical professional's opinion connecting the documented findings in this individual case
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Coexisting sensorineural loss (presbycusis, noise-induced, ototoxic) as the tinnitus generator
Somatic and temporomandibular tinnitus unrelated to the ear
Middle-ear disease (effusion, cholesteatoma) as an independent cause rather than the conductive loss identity itself
Reverse direction: tinnitus prominence driving care-seeking that reveals the conductive loss (ascertainment bias)

suggestions.rationale: Authored conservatively at association-only strength: the quantified prevalence anchor is otosclerosis-specific and severity is decoupled from hearing degree, so the edge records the documented co-occurrence and the reversible conductive-deprivation mechanism without a causal claim.
